# General background (artificial fixture)

## Reaction yield and temperature

In many batch reactions the rate constant grows with temperature (Arrhenius behaviour), so yield first rises
with temperature. At high temperature, side reactions or decomposition can lower the yield again, so the best
temperature usually depends on the reaction time as well.

## Two-variable searches

When two variables compensate each other (for example a hotter but shorter run versus a cooler but longer run),
the response surface can form a tilted ridge. Changing one variable at a time can stall on such a ridge;
moving both variables together is often more informative.

## Catalyst screening

Turnover number (TON) is the amount of product per amount of catalyst. Higher catalyst loading usually raises
conversion but can lower TON at a fixed conversion. Thermal budgets that couple temperature and residence time
are linear constraints on the allowed settings.
